{{Quote|Don't bother with them! Keep the ship in orbit!|[[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] to OOM pilot battle droids during the Battle of Coruscant|<ref name="SWE3">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
The '''OOM pilot battle droid''' was an [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM-series battle droid]] used in the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]] and, later, the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Droid Army]] for the purpose of [[Pilot/Legends|piloting]] vehicles of various kinds.

==Characteristics==
[[File:Pilot_Battle_Droids.png|thumb|left|250px|Two pilot battle droids working in the hangar of a Trade Federation Droid Control Ship.]]
The [[OOM-series battle droid/Legends|OOM]] [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]] had advanced [[Programmer/Legends|programming]] to pilot vehicles and vessels. In order to accommodate their piloting and engineering tasks, these droids had advanced specialization programming that allowed them to easily understand the control systems of any vehicle. They also carried supplies such as emergency tools and ammunition dispensers.<ref name="BF I guide">[[Star Wars Battlefront: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Battlefront'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref>

[[Baktoid Armor Workshop/Legends|Baktoid Armor Workshop]] pilot battle droids were distinguished from tan-plated [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|infantry battle droids]] by the [[Color/Legends|blue]] markings on their torsos. They stood 1.91 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall, and their black [[Sensor/Legends|sensors]] were on their cranial unit.<ref name="Databank" />

They operated anything from [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|''Providence''-class carrier/destroyers]]<ref name="SWE3" /> and [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class battleships]] to [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tanks]] and [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transports]].<ref name="JPB guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Jedi Power Battles'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> Three were part of the crew of the Armored Assault Tanks.<ref name="EG Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> OOM pilot droids also piloted [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheric]] vehicles such as the [[Conqueror-class atmospheric dreadnaught|''Conqueror''-class dreadnaught]].<ref name="Skyalkwers">{{CWACite|2|Skywalkers}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Pilotbattledroids.jpg|thumb|right|Pilot battle droids in a hangar on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]].]]
OOM pilot droids functioned mostly as the [[Starship/Legends|ships']] crews of the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]].<ref name="SWE1" />

Pilot droids were deployed throughout the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], starting from the [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|Battle of Geonosis]].<ref name="BF I" /> The droids played pivotal roles as pilots, saboteurs, and mechanics in tightly contested skirmishes of major battles such as the [[Battle of Kashyyyk/Legends|Battle of Kashyyyk]] and the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]]. They were also deployed in space battles to man turrets, carry ammunition, and monitor the decks and hangars for breaches and boarding parties. Overall, they weren't part of a separate branch but instead shared by the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|army]] and [[Confederate Navy/Legends|navy]].<ref name="BF II" /> During the Clone Wars, OOM pilot battle droids were part of the crew of [[Munificent-class star frigate/Legends|''Munificent''-class star frigates]] and took orders from organic and [[OOM command battle droid/Legends|OOM]] droid [[Commander/Legends|commanders]].<ref name="TCW">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]''</ref>

==Equipment==
[[File:Pilot battle droid BFII.jpg|thumb|right|150px|A pilot battle droid holding a SE-14 blaster pistol.]]
OOM pilot droids were deployed on battlefields and equipped with weaponry to push the assault forward. The pilot droids utilized [[RD-4 grenade launcher]]s or carried [[SE-14C blaster pistol/Legends|SE-14C blaster pistols]]. Serving as mainly support units, they often brought with them extra ammunition canisters for fellow allies, along with [[F-187 fusioncutter]] for repairs<ref name="BF I guide" /> or to cut into enemy-controlled vehicles.<ref name="BF II" />

Most pilot droids were, however, used on-board capital ships and cruisers. Some of them were armed with variants of the standard [[SE-14 blaster pistol|SE-14 blaster]], which fires more rapidly and carries greater firepower. During boarding operations against enemy [[Starship/Legends|starships]], they used [[TB-47 time bomb]]s to sabotage enemy starships.<ref name="BF II" /> When not armed, pilot droids executed only the most basic melee attacks.<ref name="JPB guide" />

==Behind the scenes==
OOM pilot battle droids first appeared with the release of the [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']] film. The OOM designation originates with the ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'', first alluded to in the ''[[Arms & Equipment Guide]]''. There, it is described as having the same processor as the OOM Commander, as exemplified by [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]] in ''The Phantom Menace'', and is first designated "OOM-Series" in ''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''.

In the [[Star Wars Battlefront (series)|''Star Wars: Battlefront'']] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] series, they serve as the pilot class for the Confederacy of Independent Systems. In the first [[Star Wars: Battlefront|Battlefront game]], pilot droids were incorrectly depicted as having no markings on their bodies, while the blue markings were worn by [[assault battle droid]]s. This was corrected in [[Star Wars: Battlefront II|the sequel]], where the pilot droids had blue markings.

The droids are also the pilots of the AAT Microfighters in the [[LEGO Star Wars|LEGO ''Star Wars'']] Microfighters tie-ins.
